award.statute: Ark. Code Ann. § 6-18-2505(a)(1) — the division shall allocate annually to each participating student's account an amount equal to ninety percent (90%) of the prior year's statewide foundation funding allotted per student. The platform fee is withheld under § 6-18-2505(e)(2)(B), which caps the withholding at five percent.
award.succeed_note: Former Succeed Scholarship participants receive 100% of the prior year's foundation funding under § 6-18-2505(a)(2). The 2024-25 annual report prints two different figures for this: $7,617 on p3 and $7,618 on p5. $7,618 is 100% of the 2023-24 foundation rate exactly, so p3 is a typo in the source. efa_state_summary.csv captured p3's figure; it is reported here as the source defect it is, not silently corrected.

atlas.rounding_note: Percentages are stored exactly as printed. Six of the fourteen published rows sum to 99 or 101 because the source rounds each of the four levels independently. They are NOT normalised to 100 — that would invent precision the source does not have.

excluded.reason: Hedged by the source as “nearly 57,000”. The approval counts from the same speaker are exact and are plotted, badged reported; this one is not, because drawing a round number the speaker hedged as a precise bar would assert a precision the source disclaims. The distinction is the number's precision, not its provenance — both come from the same department spokesperson. So the 2026-27 funnel row begins at approved, and the applications figure is quoted in words instead.

register.probe: Both annual reports searched for a demographic breakdown; neither publishes one. The application does not ask. Checked 2026-07-27.
No income data appears in either report. EFA eligibility has never been means-tested, so the programme does not gather it. Checked 2026-07-27.
Both PDFs searched for a grade-level participation breakdown; neither publishes one. Only eligibility-category, schooling-sector and prior-school-status breakdowns exist. Checked 2026-07-27.

The 2023-24 report lists a city for every participating school; the 2024-25 report's Table 1 omits city for about 83% of rows, keeping it only to disambiguate same-named campuses. No report has ever given participants' own district or county. Checked 2026-07-27.

Appendix B covers spring 2025 only. The report's own footnote states provider identities “could not be reliably determined” for autumn 2024 because of limitations in the payment platform then in use. Roughly half the year's spending has no recipient attached to it anywhere in the public record.

The 2023-24 report contains 15 dollar amounts in 28 pages, on pages 5, 7, 22, 23 and 24. None is per-school. Year-on-year growth in money received by a named school cannot be read from these reports at all.
Schools appear by name only — no code, no ID, no address — in both reports and in the expenditure appendix, where the same school is often spelled differently again. Checked 2026-07-27.
register.obtained_by: Not obtainable: the state's own private-school directory has no stable ID either, truncates school_name at 30 characters in the source database, and omits 15–23% of EFA schools entirely — including the programme's two largest recipients.

register.probe: No 2025-26 annual report exists yet (expected ~October 2026), and no interim per-school expenditure release was found. Checked 2026-07-27.
Neither annual report publishes tuition. The state collects it on the school application form. Checked 2026-07-27.
register.obtained_by: The Arkansas Advocate obtained 170 application packets under FOIA and reported an average tuition of about $9,800 for 2026-27 (1 July 2026). The figure on this page is theirs; the underlying records are the state's.

register.probe: The reports publish category totals and a recipient appendix, never the transactions themselves. The payment platform holds them. Checked 2026-07-27.
6,495 applied and 5,700 were approved in 2023-24; 18,921 applied and 14,457 were approved in 2024-25. Nothing published explains a single denial. Checked 2026-07-27.
No service-level or processing-time figure appears in either report, despite a vendor backlog being reported in mid-2026. Checked 2026-07-27.
The programme collects a norm-referenced test score and nothing else about a participating student's schooling. Checked 2026-07-27.

A complete enumeration of the Arkansas General Assembly's document server over 2023-03-01 to 2026-07-27 — 7,232 index rows, 5,932 attachments, 663 meetings, all HTTP 200, zero failures — found exactly two EFA reports filed to the legislature in 41 months, and no quarterly series. Agendas in the same window carry 171 genuine quarterly filings from other agencies, so a DESE quarterly would have appeared in the index had one been filed.

No 2025-26 annual report exists on the DESE site or the legislative server. The only 2025-26 figures in the record are the 2024-25 report's forward-looking Outlook paragraph and its retention table. Checked 2026-07-27.

No state publication held by this project contains 2026-27 participation counts: not the two annual reports, not the appropriation acts, not the DESE programme pages, not the legislative exhibit server. Checked 2026-07-27.
register.obtained_by: The Arkansas Advocate published approved counts attributed to the Department (51,041 approved — 28,096 private school, 22,945 homeschool, as of 26 June 2026) alongside school-application figures from records obtained under FOIA.

Listed here because this project's own QA twice stated no 2025-26 school-level data existed; an audit found the 2024-25 report's Table 2 measures the 2024-25 → 2025-26 transition, and both QA files now carry dated corrections.

reconciliation.detail: Averaging Table 1's own 97 per-school percentages gives 37.9%, but the same report states 39%. reconciliation.what: Every award year is 90% of the prior year's foundation funding
reconciliation.detail: Allocated amounts are computed as 0.90 × the prior year's foundation rate, not typed: $6,672 / $6,856 / $6,994 / $7,346. All four match the published figures exactly.

reconciliation.what: Tables 4 + 5 (by sector) summed against Table 3 (all students), dollars
reconciliation.detail: The same 2024-25 spending, split two ways in one report, gives two different totals. Tables 4 and 5 each reconcile to their own printed total exactly; summed, they exceed Table 3's printed total by $18,643. Nothing in either report explains the difference — Appendix A defines the expenditure categories and states no scope difference between the all-student table and the by-sector tables. Reported as found, unexplained, and not reconciled by adjusting either side.

reconciliation.what: Tables 4 + 5 (by sector) summed against Table 3 (all students), transactions
reconciliation.detail: 95,385 + 85,188 = 180,573 against Table 3's printed 180,602 — 29 transactions short, while the dollar total on the same split runs $18,643 long. The two gaps point in opposite directions, so a single omitted set of rows does not explain them.
